title: Probing wetting and solidification dynamics of neon thin films with a high-$T_c$ superconducting circuit
authors: Brennan Dizdar, Yueheng Shi, David I. Schuster, Christopher S. Lang
abstract: Integrating condensed noble gases with superconducting circuits offers new opportunities for operating hybrid quantum devices. In particular, electrons on solid neon have recently emerged as exceptionally coherent charge qubits, however the growth of the underlying neon films on patterned devices remains poorly controlled. We monitor neon films near the triple point using a multimode resonator fabricated from high-$T_c$ YBCO, which remains superconducting at temperatures where the liquid phase exists and whose geometry sets a thickness-sensing window near 1 $μ$m. In the liquid state we observe rich film dynamics: uniform wetting that saturates near 20 nm, drainage of thicker films, and spontaneous thickness oscillations, reflecting the extreme sensitivity of thick films in this regime. A galvanic connection to our sensing volume enables in-situ electrostatic tuning of the liquid film thickness. Statistics of freezing the neon across various liquid levels reveal variations of the solid film thickness by approximately an order of magnitude. We also observe a two-fold increase in the quality factor of the resonators at the level of $10^3$ with added neon and rule out dielectric loss as the limiting factor. Our results demonstrate that hermetic packaging facilitates the investigation of both rich non-equilibrium fluid dynamics and the impact of condensed noble gas films on microwave loss in superconducting circuits, but may not be the best modality for growing solid neon films with precisely controlled thickness.
summary: This work uses a superconducting resonator to study how liquid and solid neon films interact with microwave circuits. By monitoring changes in resonance frequency and quality factor, the authors characterize the non-equilibrium fluid dynamics of neon wetting and solidification. The results are crucial for understanding the environmental coupling and loss mechanisms in next-generation hybrid quantum devices.
main_problem: The study investigates the wetting and solidification dynamics of neon thin films and quantifies the impact of these condensed noble gas films on the microwave loss properties of superconducting circuits.
main_result: The experiment successfully characterized rich non-equilibrium fluid dynamics, observing distinct wetting regimes and quantifying the increase in resonator quality factor ($Q_L$) upon neon deposition, while noting limitations in precise solid film thickness control.
method: Measurements involve monitoring the resonance frequency shift ($\Delta f$) and loaded quality factor ($Q_L$) of a superconducting resonator as neon is introduced or allowed to freeze in a controlled, hermetic environment.
model_or_system: The physical system is a voltage-tunable, multimode coplanar stripline resonator made of high-$T_c$ YBCO, housed in a cell near the neon triple point. The analysis uses electromagnetic simulations (Ansys Maxwell) to model the frequency shift based on the dielectric properties of the liquid and solid neon films.
key_observables: Resonance frequency shift ($\Delta f$), loaded quality factor ($Q_L$), and film thickness ($t$) across various wetting regimes (I-IV).
important_parameters: Neon film thickness (ranging from saturation levels near 20 nm to larger amounts), temperature near the triple point (24.56 K), and the dielectric constants of liquid ($\epsilon_r \approx 1.19$) and solid ($\epsilon_r \approx 1.24$) neon.
main_assumptions: The analysis often assumes uniform film coverage across the resonator surface, and the dielectric loss model alone is insufficient to explain the observed increase in $Q_L$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the setup (hermetic cell, resonator schematic), the frequency shift evolution across four distinct liquid filling regimes (I-IV), and the dependence of $Q_L$ on neon thickness for both liquid and solid states.
paper_structure: The paper details the experimental setup, presents measurements of frequency shifts and $Q_L$ as a function of neon dosing/temperature, analyzes the observed non-equilibrium fluid dynamics, and discusses the implications for superconducting circuit performance.
why_interesting: The work bridges condensed matter physics (fluid dynamics, phase transitions) with superconducting circuit QED, providing empirical data on how ambient quantum materials interact with highly sensitive quantum devices.
